newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil court delays controversial pay ruling.
newsitem.headline: Brazil court delays controversial pay ruling.

text.p: Brazil's most senior court postponed a ruling on a controversial pay issue which the government fears might undermine its drive to keep a tight grip on the federal payroll, an official said.

The Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF) did not rule on the issue on Thursday as scheduled because a judge in charge of the case was absent from Brasilia and no new date for a ruling has been set, an STF spokeswoman said.

The case was brought by 11 civil servants who claim they are entitled to a 28.9 percent pay rise given to the armed forces in 1993. The civil servants cite a rule that entitles public sector workers to pay raises awarded to state employees in other categories.
Government officials say a victory for the 11 might set a precedent for the entire federal workforce.
Newspapers have said an across-the-board pay rise of 28.9 percent could add $7.0 billion to the federal government's payroll spending, expected to total about $42 billion in 1996.
